This was a retrospective cohort study that included neonates with HIE admitted to a level IV NICU for therapeutic hypothermia comparing two dexmedetomidine dosing regimens: (1) pre-implementation: starting dose of 0.05 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.05 μg/kg/h every 6 h as needed, and (2) post-implementation: 0.2 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.1 μg/kg/h every 30-60 min as needed. A total of 106 neonates were included: 50 in the pre-implementation group and 56 in the post-implementation group. Compliance to post-implementation formulary recommendations was 69.6% for initial doses, 62.5% for dose increases, and 44.6% for dose decreases. An increased odds of opioid exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 7.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.59-51.5, p = 0.02) and greater proportion of bradycardia (21.4% vs. 4%, p = 0.03) were observed in the post-implementation group. No significant differences in effectiveness end points or hypotension were observed between groups (p ≥ 0.05). Compliance with formulary-recommended dexmedetomidine dosing was variable and dose decreases were common in the post-implementation group. The post-implementation dosing approach was not associated with improved effectiveness outcomes (sedation) but was associated with greater opioid exposure and more bradycardia, supporting the need for further prospective evaluation to determine the optimal dexmedetomidine dosing in neonates undergoing HIE.

title: Cognitive Correlations With Cholinergic Signaling in Parkinson Disease Depend on Global Cognitive Status.
journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
abstract: To determine the cholinergic pathway differences in Parkinson disease (PD) and healthy controls and whether correlations between cholinergic function and cognitive domains within PD relate to global cognitive status. Cholinergic activity was measured in PD (N = 50) and control (N = 28) participants using the vesicular cholinergic transporter PET tracer, [18F]VAT. Scans were reconstructed and partial volume corrected. Regional binding potentials were calculated using the multilinear reference tissue model 2 (MRTM2). Global cognitive status was assessed using the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) scale with PD participants stratified as cognitively intact (CDR = 0, N = 28) and cognitively impaired (CDR = 0.5, N = 22). Cognitive performance was measured across attention, memory, language, visuospatial, and executive function domains. Regions of interest (ROIs) were defined using all PD and control participants, identifying regions with [18F]VAT-cognitive domain correlations for subgroup analyses. PD participants demonstrated significantly lower [18F]VAT binding relative to controls but not between PD subgroups. [18F]VAT correlations were identified in whole-group analysis for attention and visuospatial function. Stepwise linear regression revealed significant regional associations between [18F]VAT and attention for the whole-PD group and both attention and visuospatial function for the cognitively impaired PD group. In fact, the PD group with cognitive impairment exhibited strong correlations (r > 0.5, 5% FDR) between [18F]VAT and visuospatial function in almost all ROIs. These results demonstrate that the relationship between cholinergic signaling and visuospatial function differs based on global cognitive status in PD. Significant differences in VAT binding across the full PD sample suggest that cholinergic denervation precedes cognitive impairment in PD and imply other compensatory mechanisms may exist in cognitively intact participants but this needs confirmation in longitudinal analysis.

title: CaMKII generates actin bundle morphology and mechanics distinct from canonical bivalent cross-linkers.
abstract: Actin cross-linkers are essential modulators of the actin cytoskeleton, enabling structural diversity and dynamic remodeling. Among them, calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) is unique in serving a dual role as a kinase and as a multivalent structural binder of actin in dendritic spines, where it plays a major role in supporting dendritic spine structure via its β subunit. To understand the basis of the structural function of CaMKII, we quantified the morphology and mechanics of actin bundles formed by CaMKII and directly compared them with bundles assembled by the canonical bivalent cross-linkers α-actinin and fascin. Using fluorescence microscopy, we measured contour length, straightness ratio, and persistence length across different cross-linker concentrations. Fascin generated progressively shorter, straighter, and stiffer bundles with increasing concentration, whereas α-actinin bundles remained largely unchanged. In contrast, increasing CaMKII concentration reduced both bundle straightness and persistence length, revealing a unique concentration-dependent increase in bundle flexibility. To investigate the structural origins of these mechanical behaviors, we complemented the experiments with coarse-grained simulations of cross-linked actin bundles. Simulations revealed that CaMKII-generated bundles retained a substantially larger fraction of their curvature in their time-averaged configuration than bundles formed by α-actinin or fascin, indicating that bundle mechanics are strongly influenced by organizational features beyond thermal bending fluctuations alone. CaMKII bundles displayed behavior consistent with additional structural complexity arising from their multivalent architecture and flexible linker domains. Together, our experimental and computational results identify CaMKII as a structurally and mechanically distinct actin cross-linker. We propose that the combination of multivalency and linker flexibility enables CaMKII to function as a molecular structural pivot, promoting flexible, adaptable actin assemblies that are mechanically compatible with the dynamic remodeling required for dendritic spine plasticity.

title: Chronic Oral Trehalose Intake Induces Sex-Dependent Hippocampal Dysfunction and Cognitive Impairment in Healthy Mice.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
abstract: Trehalose is a naturally occurring nonreducing disaccharide widely distributed across diverse organisms, where it serves as both a stress protectant and an energy source. Although vertebrates lack the ability to synthesize trehalose, its expanding use in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic industries has led to a marked, unintentional increase in dietary intake. In mammals, trehalose is only partially hydrolyzed, and emerging evidence indicates that a fraction of unmetabolized trehalose can enter systemic circulation, cross the blood-brain barrier, and influence metabolic processes, gut microbiota composition, and potentially brain function. Notably, trehalose has been identified as an inducer of autophagy and has shown efficacy in several models of neurodegenerative diseases. Given its increasing consumption and potential impact on the central nervous system, this study investigates the effects of chronic oral trehalose intake in healthy mice. Using a multidisciplinary approach encompassing behavioral analyses, metabolomics, and ex vivo and in vivo assessments of neuronal function, we demonstrate that prolonged trehalose consumption impairs spatial cognition and associative memory and induces structural, functional, and lipidomic alterations in the brain. These effects exhibit a marked sex-dependent pattern, predominantly affecting male mice. Importantly, these changes occur without significant modulation of autophagy in the brain, suggesting that alternative mechanisms may underlie the observed effects of trehalose on neuronal physiology. Overall, despite its widespread use and GRAS classification, prolonged trehalose intake may adversely affect brain physiology and cognition in a sex-dependent manner.

title: Sleep-Deprivation Serum Induces Mitochondrial Stress in BV2 Cells: Responses to P2Y12-Targeted Pharmacological Modulation.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) disrupts neuroimmune and metabolic homeostasis, but whether circulating factors generated after sleep loss alter microglial responses to purinergic pharmacological modulation remains unclear. P2Y12 is a microglia-enriched purinergic receptor that regulates process dynamics, calcium signaling, and microglial interactions with neurons and vascular-glial interfaces. Here, we established an in vitro serum-transfer model to test whether serum from sleep-deprived mice alters mitochondrial and Rhod-2 fluorescence responses to P2Y12-targeted compounds in BV2 cells. Mice were subjected to forced-wheel SD consisting of one wheel revolution every 2 s for 4 h per day over 4 consecutive days, and serum was obtained by cardiac blood collection followed by centrifugation. BV2 cells were treated with control or SD serum in the absence or presence of the P2Y12 antagonist MRS2395 or the P2Y12 agonist 2-MeSADP. Mitochondrial membrane potential was assessed by JC-1 red/green ratio imaging, mitochondrial network integrity by MitoTracker-based segmentation and skeletonization, and Rhod-2 fluorescence responses by single-cell F/F0 imaging. SD serum decreased the JC-1 ratio, increased maximal depolarization, reduced mitochondrial skeleton length and mitochondrial area fraction, and suppressed Rhod-2 responses. Under control-serum conditions, MRS2395 markedly enhanced Rhod-2 responses, whereas the increase in the area under the Rhod-2 response curve with 2-MeSADP was not significant after Holm correction. Under SD-serum conditions, however, neither compound consistently restored the mitochondrial or Rhod-2 response profile. Together, these findings link SD-serum exposure to mitochondrial impairment and attenuated Rhod-2 fluorescence responses in BV2 cells, and suggest that serum context may influence cellular responses to P2Y12-targeted compounds.

title: Regulatory T and Activated T Cells in the Chronic Unpredictable Mild Stress Mice: Sex Differences and Effects of Treatments.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with immune dysregulation, including T-cell activation and reduced regulatory T cells. Pharmacological treatments like fluoxetine, simvastatin, curcumin, and S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) show promise in alleviating depressive symptoms, but their effects on immune responses are not fully understood. This study explored immune status in MDD using the chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model. It examined how fluoxetine, simvastatin, curcumin, and SAMe affected immune responses and depressive behaviors. The study also investigated sex differences. Six groups, each with 12 mice (6 males and 6 females), were included: control, CUMS and drug treatments. Male and female mice were housed separately in sex-specific cages throughout the experiment, with three mice per cage. Behavioral tests included sucrose preference, forced swimming, open field and active avoidance. Immune cell markers were analyzed by flow cytometry. CUMS mice showed immune imbalance, with Treg depletion (p = 0.047) and a higher CD154/CD152 ratio (p = 0.006). All treatments improved depressive-like behaviors (all p < 0.05), with SAMe normalizing the CD154/CD152 ratio (p = 0.009). Furthermore, female mice exhibited lower levels of Treg-related immune regulation and T-cell activation compared to males (both p < 0.001), along with a higher CD154/CD152 ratio (p = 0.008). This study highlights that curcumin, simvastatin, fluoxetine, and SAMe alleviate depressive-like behaviors, while SAMe also reduces the CD154/CD152 ratio. These findings reveal marked sex differences in T-cell activation and immune regulation, highlighting the importance of considering sex as a biological variable in CUMS research.

title: Cortical Topology Organization in Virally Suppressed HIV and Its Cognitive Relevance: A Morphometric Similarity Network Study.
abstract: People living with HIV (PLWH) commonly exhibit region-specific disruptions in cortical gray matter. However, the clinical relevance of structural brain network topology in virally suppressed PLWH remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of HIV on cortical network topology using morphometric similarity networks (MSNs) and evaluated whether concurrent marijuana use modulates these effects. We also assessed associations between network graph measures and neurocognitive performance. A total of 239 adult participants were enrolled and stratified by HIV and marijuana status (61 control, 53 marijuana-only, 63 HIV-only, 62 HIV + marijuana). MSNs were generated from high-resolution anatomical MRI collected alongside neuropsychological battery. We analyzed differences in network resilience, centrality, integration, segregation, and overall topological balance (integration-segregation difference, or ISD) as a function of HIV and marijuana use. Statistical tests further assessed relationships between network measures and cognitive outcomes. Participants had a mean age of 38.19 years, and all PLWH had sustained viral suppression. Participants with HIV showed significant alterations in brain network organization compared to participants without HIV, whereas no main or interactive effects of marijuana use were detected. PLWH demonstrated higher segregation and lower integration-segregation balance (indexed by ISD). Exploratory analyses identified modest associations between network measures and cognitive performance among PLWH, such that lower ISD was associated with better cognitive performance. These findings suggest that HIV infection is associated with altered morphometric network organization, even under effective viral suppression. The association of MSN topology with cognitive performance may suggest a potential preliminary relationship between cortical morphometric network organization and cognitive functioning in chronic HIV. Future longitudinal and multimodal studies are needed to determine whether these network properties can predict the cognitive trajectories in this population.

title: Neuroprotective Mechanisms of Electroacupuncture at Baihui (GV20) in Experimental Ischemic Stroke: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Ischemic stroke is a major cause of death and disability, and reperfusion therapy has a narrow time window and may cause further injury after recanalization. Baihui (GV20) is the acupoint used most often in experimental studies of acupuncture for stroke, and electroacupuncture (EA) at GV20, applied alone or combined with other acupoints, has been tested in a large body of animal work. Taking GV20 as its organizing focus, this review systematically summarizes the mechanisms by which GV20-based EA protects against ischemic stroke in animal models. GV20-based EA has been reported to reduce neuroinflammation through the α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor-high-mobility group box 1 pathway, nuclear factor-κB and inflammasome signaling, and glial responses; to prevent apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis and engage adenosine A1 receptor signaling; to preserve mitochondrial dynamics, energy metabolism, and redox balance; to protect the blood-brain barrier and promote cerebral perfusion and angiogenesis; and to enhance neurotrophic signaling, synaptic plasticity, and white matter repair. GV20 alone has been studied mainly as preconditioning, and GV20-based combinations have been applied primarily after ischemia; the effects on hypoxia-inducible factor-1α, autophagy, and microglial polarization vary with the timing of EA and assessment. Because these findings derive largely from young, healthy rodents and most mechanistic results are based on changes in expression, they do not yet support direct clinical application; future studies should compare GV20 alone with GV20-based combinations under the same conditions and validate key mechanisms with causal designs in clinically relevant models.

title: Carbon Monoxide-Releasing Nanoreactors Transiently Modulate TLR4 Signaling to Resolve Inflammation.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Uncontrolled inflammation drives diverse acute and chronic diseases, yet effective suppression without compromising host defense remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization. Here, we report a metal-free micellar nanoreactor that implements a nanoconfined cascade between endoperoxides (EPOs) and 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) derivatives for sustained CO generation. Thermal decomposition of EPOs continuously produces singlet oxygen (1O2), which subsequently oxidizes adjacent CO precursors to release CO with programmable kinetics under physiological conditions. Systematic molecular screening revealed that the cascade kinetics are governed by the structures of the EPOs as well as aromatic-ring extension and chalcogen substitution within the 3-HF scaffold, enabling oxidation rates to be tuned over 3 orders of magnitude. Relative to an equivalent mixture of separately assembled micelles, coassembly accelerated S-HF oxidation and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with more efficient capture of the short-lived 1O2 intermediate within the micellar core. Sustained intracellular CO generation transiently decreased surface-detectable TLR4/MD-2, attenuated downstream inflammatory signaling and cytokine amplification, and promoted macrophage repolarization, while TLR4/MD-2 levels subsequently returned toward baseline. The nanoreactors alleviated inflammation and tissue injury in mouse models of APAP-induced acute liver injury, LPS-induced endotoxemia, and allergic airway inflammation. These findings establish an autonomous, nanoconfined reaction cascade for sustained gasotransmitter delivery and transient modulation of pathological inflammation.

title: Twenty Years of the Concept of the Privileged Extracellular Region: From Early Computations to Modern Anatomical Evidence.
abstract: The brain extracellular space (ECS) is a heterogeneous and plastic compartment. The concept of the privileged extracellular region (PER) was introduced in 2004 as a computationally derived, spatially restricted microdomain of the ECS immediately surrounding glial cells, within which potassium (K+) accumulates preferentially and independently from the broader extracellular milieu. Using mathematical modeling of membrane currents in astrocytes and oligodendrocytes, the seminal paper demonstrated that the volume of the ECS accessible for K+ accumulation during depolarization was 10-100-fold smaller around oligodendrocytes than around astrocytes, establishing the first quantitative evidence for spatial heterogeneity of the periglial ECS. Over the following two decades, converging lines of structural, functional, and clinical evidence have dramatically expanded this concept. Perisynaptic astrocytic regions and extracellular geometry have now been visualized at nanoscale resolution using STED, dSTORM, and super-resolution shadow imaging (SUSHI), revealing a spongiform architecture with fine leaflets and reflexive loops that delineate functionally distinct microdomains at the synaptic interface. EAAT2/GLT-1 glutamate transporters and Kir4.1 K+ channels concentrated within these processes provide the molecular infrastructure for localized neurotransmitter clearance and K+ siphoning. Disruption of PER geometry-through reactive gliosis, astrocytic atrophy during aging, or leaflet retraction-contributes to the pathophysiology of epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, ischemia, and cognitive decline. The present review traces the intellectual lineage of the PER concept, integrates two decades of anatomical and functional evidence, and highlights the therapeutic implications of understanding periglial microdomains as active regulators of brain homeostasis.

title: Brain Region-Specific Expression of m6A Regulatory Enzymes in the Inflammation-Induced Mouse Model of Anxiety.
abstract: Peripheral inflammation induces anxiety-like and sickness behaviors, yet the underlying epitranscriptomic correlates remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the regional transcriptional alterations of key N6-methyladenosine (m6A) regulatory enzymes across the limbic system in response to systemic immune challenge. Systemic inflammation was induced in mice via lipopolysaccharide (LPS) administration, followed by the evaluation of behavioral paradigms for anxiety-like and sickness behaviors. We subsequently mapped the mRNA expression profiles of major m6A writers, erasers, and readers across critical limbic brain regions and performed correlational analyses between these transcriptional changes and specific behavioral indices. Inflammatory challenge triggered distinct, region-specific alterations in m6A regulators. Notably, while FTO was downregulated in both the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and hippocampus, its behavioral associations diverged: only NAc FTO correlated with anxiety-like phenotypes, and FTO exhibited opposite correlations with feeding between these two regions. Furthermore, molecular specificity was observed in the basolateral amygdala (BLA); despite the downregulation of both METTL3 and METTL14, only METTL14 significantly correlated with feeding and anxiety-like behaviors. The mRNA expression of major m6A regulatory enzymes exhibits complex, brain-region-specific patterns that strongly correlate with distinct behavioral outputs during inflammation. These observational findings provide a conceptual framework indicating that regional epitranscriptomic machinery is closely associated with behavioral specificity, highlighting promising transcriptional targets for future functional and mechanistic validation in anxiolytic interventions.

title: Linking Research Outputs to Support Transparency and Reproducibility in Preclinical Traumatic Brain Injury Studies: A Live Implementation Experience.
abstract: The PRE-Clinical Interagency reSearch resourcE-Traumatic Brain Injury (PRECISE-TBI) is a community-based consortium developing standards, resources, and tools to support preclinical traumatic brain injury (TBI) research. PRECISE-TBI aims to address barriers that contribute to the translational gap by improving transparency, interoperability, and accessibility of preclinical TBI data and methods. The PRECISE-TBI Education Focus Area develops and curates resources relevant to blast-related research, working with the broader community to address issues pertinent to both military and civilian populations. Using two complementary implementation examples, we illustrate the practical application of current PRECISE-TBI resources in preclinical TBI research, including the coordinated use of the Model Catalog and the Open Data Commons for TBI (ODC-TBI) repository. Together, these components form an integrated, FAIR-aligned publication and data sharing framework tailored to preclinical TBI research. We further describe a linked research output publication workflow, whereas traditional research articles are complemented by executable protocols hosted on protocols.io and curated, machine-readable datasets published as independent digital objects. This linked collection of research outputs has been referred to as the "Paper of the Future" in related PRECISE-TBI publications. These resources adhere to Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable principles through the use of persistent identifiers, rich metadata, and mapping to the community-defined Common Data Elements. This use case illustrates how PRECISE-TBI-aligned practices can facilitate compliance with the NIH Data Management and Sharing policy and provide a structured approach to documenting experimental design, provenance, and data limitations in preclinical TBI research. While this study does not evaluate downstream outcomes, the framework is intended to enable future assessment of data reuse, harmonization, and reproducibility by making research outputs transparent, citable, and evaluable through persistent cross-linking of publications, protocols, and datasets.

title: Stress Granules in Health and Disease: From Adaptive RNA Triage to Pathological Persistence.
abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein (RNP) condensates that assemble when translation initiation is inhibited during stress. Classically viewed as transient sites of mRNA triage, SGs are now recognized as heterogeneous assemblies whose composition, material properties, and recovery capacity vary with the stressor, cell type, RNA substrate, and clearance pathway. SG assembly involves the selective recruitment of untranslated RNPs, followed by nucleation and maturation. SG disassembly is an active process in which translational restart, protein remodeling, and degradative pathways influence whether SG components return to function or are targeted for degradation. In neurodegenerative disease, prolonged residence of SG-associated RNAs and proteins may prevent their return to normal function and favor persistent or aberrant RNP states. In this Review, we propose that SGs are more informatively defined by mechanism and molecular state than by marker positivity alone. We organize SG biology along a continuum from acute, adaptive RNA triage to chronic, persistent SG-like assemblies. This framework helps reconcile the distinct relationships between SGs and different neurodegenerative diseases. It also distinguishes persistent, poorly resolved SG-like states as potential disease-relevant targets from physiological SGs that function as adaptive stress-response compartments.

title: Inhibition of oxytocin neurons during key periods of development has long-term behavioral and body composition effects.
abstract: Oxytocin (OT) is a key neuromodulator of social behavior in mammals, and accumulating evidence supports the existence of a critical period for OT action during infancy. However, other developmental windows remain poorly explored, and it remains unclear whether OT exerts distinct functions depending on the timing of its activity. In this study, we aimed to determine whether specific developmental stages exist during which OT-expressing neurons play a decisive role with long-term consequences. We used a chemogenetic approach to transiently inhibit OT-expressing neurons during three postnatal developmental periods: infancy, the juvenile period, and young adulthood in male and female mice. Behavioral and metabolic outcomes were then assessed longitudinally. We also examined the effects of inhibiting OT neurons during late fetal stages and at birth. Social memory was consistently impaired in males, regardless of the timing of neuronal inactivation. The most pronounced behavioral effects were observed following inhibition during infancy in both sexes. Metabolically, adult males from all cohorts exhibited increased body weight, whereas increased fat mass and adipocyte size hypertrophy were specifically observed following inhibition during the juvenile period. Notably, inhibition of OT-expressing neurons around the time of birth resulted in delayed parturition and altered neonatal feeding behavior. OT-expressing neurons release multiple signaling molecules. However, converging evidence suggests that the observed phenotypes are primarily attributable to OT deficiency. Although this study demonstrates long-term behavioral and metabolic consequences of transient OT neuron inhibition, further experiments are required to elucidate underlying mechanisms and identify additional effects. Transient inhibition of OT-expressing neurons during distinct postnatal developmental periods leads to long-lasting effects on social behavior and metabolism, with outcomes depending on both the timing of inhibition and sex. Furthermore, our findings reveal an unexpected role for fetal/neonatal OT neurons in regulating the timing of birth and early feeding behavior.

title: Neuron-enriched STAT4 shapes time- and context-dependent neuronal outcomes in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly linked to dynamic and context-dependent alterations in intracellular signaling. However, how these changes drive progressive neurodegeneration and divergent neuronal outcomes remains poorly understood. Integrative analyses across independent human single-nucleus RNA sequencing datasets were performed to identify neuronal factors consistently altered in AD. Signal transducer and activator of transcription 4 (STAT4) distribution in different cell types was further validated using a mouse single-cell RNA sequencing dataset and experimental models. Functions of STAT4 were examined in human SH-SY5Y cells, mouse HT22 neuronal cells, mouse primary neurons, and inducible systems. In vivo effects were assessed in 3×Tg-AD and wild-type mice with AAV-mediated Stat4 modulation and pharmacological ERK inhibition. Multi-omics approaches, including RNA-seq, Cut&Tag, and RIP-seq, were used to explore downstream regulatory mechanisms. Integrative analyses identified STAT4 as a neuron-enriched factor consistently reduced in AD neurons. STAT4 supported neuronal integrity and synaptic homeostasis under basal conditions. Inducible restoration of STAT4 expression exerted divergent effects in a time-dependent manner, with early adaptive responses transitioning to later oxidative stress- and apoptosis-associated changes. Sustained STAT4 restoration induced oxidative stress, apoptosis-related signaling, and tau protein-related alterations, which were attenuated by ERK inhibition. In contrast, the beneficial outputs, including reduced Aβ burden and improved synaptic and neuronal markers, were preserved despite ERK inhibition. Parallel analyses in wild-type mice showed a delayed trajectory, indicating disease-context-dependent modulation. STAT4 was further associated with coordinated signaling networks and hnRNPK-related regulatory complexes. These findings define a time- and context-dependent signaling framework in which STAT4-associated outputs progressively shift toward maladaptive, ERK-sensitive responses in AD. Selective constraint of the late-stage signaling imbalance may attenuate the pathological outcomes while preserving the beneficial effects, providing a potential strategy for context-specific therapeutic intervention.

title: Neurobiological correlates of longitudinal grey matter volume changes in preclinical Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Structural brain changes during the earliest asymptomatic stages of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain poorly understood. Previous research in preclinical AD shows heterogeneous findings, reporting both subtle neuronal loss and paradoxical increases in grey matter (GM) volume. This study applies an extensive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker panel to better understand the biological processes underlying longitudinal GM changes in cognitively unimpaired (CU) adults, spanning the amyloid/tau (AT) continuum. We analysed data from 627 CU individuals from three longitudinal cohorts (ALFA+, Wisconsin ADRC, WRAP), with repeated MRI (3.5 ± 0.9 years) and baseline CSF biomarkers from the NeuroToolKit panel (Roche Diagnostics). Using non-negative matrix factorization, we decomposed the CSF biomarker levels into six latent components, reflecting amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology, tau-related pathophysiology with synaptic injury, neuroaxonal injury, microglial reactivity, astrocytic reactivity, and cytokine signalling. We tested associations between component weights and voxel-wise longitudinal GM volume changes using single-component and a joint-all components model. Analyses were performed across the full sample and stratified by AT status. Associations with longitudinal cognitive performance (PACC) were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. The Aβ pathology component was the strongest and most widespread predictor of longitudinal GM atrophy, predominantly in temporal and frontal regions, also when controlling for tau pathophysiology, neuroaxonal injury, or neuroinflammatory components. Higher Aβ pathology scores were also associated with cognitive decline. The component capturing tau-related pathophysiology and synaptic injury initially associated with GM loss but lost significance after accounting for other biomarker components. In contrast, components reflecting microglial reactivity, astrocytic reactivity, and cytokine signalling were associated with longitudinal GM volume increases, with effects varying by AT stage. In this large longitudinal sample of asymptomatic individuals, the Aβ-dominant biomarker component showed the strongest association with longitudinal GM atrophy and cognitive decline, beyond the effects of tau pathophysiology and neuroaxonal injury. While glial and inflammatory processes may contribute to transient GM increases in preclinical AD. A better understanding of these dynamic relationships between structural brain changes and various biological pathways at the earliest stages of AD is crucial to inform the development of interventions before irreversible neurodegeneration occurs.

title: Dynamic 5-hydroxymethylcytosine remodeling associated with synaptic gene programs in the striatum of a Parkinson's disease mouse model.
abstract: The striatum, a key structure within the basal ganglia, undergoes functional dysregulation following the loss of dopaminergic input, contributing to the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD). However, the involvement of DNA hydroxymethylation in striatal dysfunction remains poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize striatal 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) profiles and their associations with transcriptional changes across two post-lesion stages in a 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) mouse model of PD. We profiled the genome-wide 5hmC landscape and transcriptome in the lesioned and contralateral striata of male mice at day 10 and day 30 after unilateral 6-OHDA injection. Global 5hmC levels were lower in the lesioned than in the contralateral striatum at day 10 but higher at day 30. Lesion-associated 5hmC remodeling and transcriptional responses were time-dependent. Functional enrichment linked genes associated with differentially hydroxymethylated regions (DhMRs) to neuronal and synaptic processes, with distinct functional profiles across time points and interaction directions. Integration of the hydroxymethylome and transcriptome suggested different patterns of association between 5hmC remodeling and gene expression in separate analyses at day 10 and day 30, with this correspondence appearing more evident at day 10. At both time points, the gene sets with concordant hydroxymethylation and expression changes were enriched for synapse-related processes, suggesting a shared synaptic functional theme across the hydroxymethylome and transcriptome. Among the TET family members, only TET1 showed temporal changes in abundance that paralleled striatal 5hmC dynamics. Together, these findings demonstrate dynamic remodeling of striatal 5hmC in male mice following 6-OHDA lesioning and identify associations between hydroxymethylation changes and synaptic gene programs, providing insight into the epigenetic features of PD-associated striatal dysfunction.

title: CT-based radiomics for interpretable outcome prediction after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: Prognostic assessment after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) mainly relies on clinical variables and computed tomography (CT) findings, but current models often lack biological interpretability. We developed and validated a clinical-radiomics prognostic model and subsequently performed exploratory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomic characterization of model-defined risk phenotypes. This multicenter cohort from the PROSAH-MPC registry included 879 patients across four hospitals. Patients from the primary center were split into training (n = 637) and internal validation (n = 160) cohorts, while patients from three other centers formed an external validation cohort (n = 82). Admission CT hemorrhagic lesions were automatically segmented using the validated BrainHemoAI platform, and radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics. Clinical, radiomics, and combined clinical-radiomics XGBoost models were developed and interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Risk scores from the clinical-radiomics model were applied to an independent prospective enrichment, gene setCSF​ proteomic cohort to define combined model-based high- and low-risk groups. Gene Ontology (GO)/ Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses were performed. The combined model yielded AUCs of 0.892 and 0.820 in the internal test and external validation cohorts, respectively. Risk reclassification analyses suggested that radiomic features may provide complementary prognostic information. SHAP identified radiomic heterogeneity and key clinical variables as major predictors. Meanwhile, exploratory CSF proteomic analysis identified candidate differentially expressed proteins and associated pathway signals that differed between groups defined by high and low combined clinical-radiomics risk scores. This clinical-radiomics prognostic model enables accurate outcome prediction and provides exploratory biological insight into unfavorable recovery after aSAH, supporting refined risk stratification and potential targeted therapeutic development. PROSAH-MPC. NCT05738083. Registered 16 November 2022 - Retrospectively registered, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05738083 .

title: Brief guided written exposure therapy for PTSD and complex PTSD in adolescents: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is prevalent among adolescents, yet evidence-based treatments remain inaccessible to most. Complex PTSD (CPTSD), recently recognized in ICD-11, lacks empirical evidence to guide intervention in this population. Guided Written Exposure (GWE) is a brief, non-phased trauma-focused treatment with established efficacy in adults. This pilot trial evaluated the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of group-delivered GWE for adolescent PTSD and CPTSD. Fifty-three adolescents (aged 13-17) with PTSD symptoms following diverse trauma exposures were randomized to five-session group GWE (n = 27) or waitlist (n = 26). Primary outcomes were PTSD and CPTSD symptoms. Secondary outcomes included depression, anxiety, and affective and behavioral problems. Assessments occurred at baseline, post-intervention, 1-month, and 3-month (GWE only) follow-up. Treatment effects were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. GWE produced significantly greater reductions than waitlist in PTSD (d = - 1.15, 95% CI [- 1.89, - 0.41]) and CPTSD symptoms (d = - 0.97, 95% CI [- 1.70, - 0.23]) at post-treatment, with gains maintained through 3-month follow-up. Depression and affective and behavioral problems also improved significantly. Retention was high (92.6%) with no adverse events. Anxiety did not differ between groups. Group-delivered GWE demonstrates promise as a brief, scalable intervention for posttraumatic stress symptoms, particularly in low-resource settings, and provides preliminary support that non-phased trauma-focused approaches may be feasible for adolescents with CPTSD. Replication in larger trials is warranted. ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06403449). Registered on 3 May 2024.

title: Joy and compassion as prosocial antidotes to aggression: an experimental comparison.
journal: Borderline personality disorder and emotion dysregulation
abstract: Aggression is a key factor in various mental health problems including personality disorders, underscoring the importance of effective interventions for regulating or preventing aggression. Positive psychology suggests that promoting prosocial emotions such as joy and compassion may help to buffer against aggression. This experimental study examined (1) whether joy- or compassion-based writing exercises can buffer against anger and aggression in response to provocation, (2) whether trait prevention focus (a self-regulation style focused on avoiding negative outcomes) influences these effects, and (3) how positive and negative affect evolve over time. A total of N = 148 university students were randomly assigned to one of three writing interventions: joy, compassion, or a procedural control. After the writing task, participants were provoked by exposing them to unsolvable anagrams and a standardized provocation by a condescending confederate. Measures of anger, positive affect (PA), and negative affect (NA) were collected at baseline, post-intervention, and post-provocation. Behavioral aggression was assessed post-provocation, using the competitive reaction time task (CRTT). Controlling for baseline levels, neither joy or compassion significantly buffered against increased anger, NA, and behavioral aggression, or against decreased PA after provocation, compared to the control condition. However, affective trajectories differed by condition: In the joy condition, post-intervention PA was significantly higher (compared to the control condition) and NA significantly lower (compared to compassion and control). However, following provocation, PA dropped and NA rose significantly more sharply in the joy condition compared to the other conditions. Prevention focus did not moderate any outcomes. These findings suggest that brief joy and compassion interventions do not buffer against aggression. Compared to inducing compassion, inducing joy does lead to more immediate improved affect, though this impact is only short-lived, potentially illustrating an affective contrast effect. More research is needed to further explore timing, contrast, and longer-term mood effects of prosocial interventions as antidotes to aggression.

title: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification in muscle stem cells and skeletal muscle regeneration.
abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is a highly conserved posttranscriptional modification essential for gene expression, cellular function, and the determination of stem cell fates. As a result, it is regulated by a variety of mechanisms and remains a promising field of study. m6A RNA methylation is mediated by multiple classes of proteins, known as writers, erasers, and readers, which are in turn controlled by various transcription factors and regulatory pathways. Dysregulation of these fundamental processes is implicated in a wide range of diseases and disorders, exemplifying their importance in guiding normal physiological activity. In this review, we focused on the effects of m6A modification on muscle stem cells (MuSCs), also known as satellite cells, a critical component of skeletal muscle development and regeneration. Further, we evaluated the contemporary literature and expert perspectives to outline the mechanisms of m6A RNA methylation, emphasizing their roles in MuSCs and their potential for developing novel therapeutic strategies.

title: Apathy in older adults is associated with selective overweighting of effort during decisions between everyday activities.
abstract: Apathy, characterized by reduced motivation and goal-directed behavior, is common in normal aging and may arise from biased cost-benefit evaluation during decision making. While prior research has focused on simple choices involving the trade-off between motor or cognitive effort and monetary reward, real-life decisions of people with apathy likely reflect biases affecting many other dimensions of value. Additionally, the extent to which mood symptoms that frequently co-occur with apathy also contribute to biases in decision making is unclear. To address these gaps, we developed a novel online task completed by 158 older adults who rated everyday activities (e.g., watching TV, going to the park) across 19 value attributes (e.g., enjoyment, social obligation), and made a series of choices between different activities. A factor analysis of attribute ratings identified three latent factors representing reward, effort, and obligation, which strongly predicted choices and choice response times. Apathy was selectively associated with an overweighting of effort-related attributes while controlling for impulsivity and depressive symptoms, with no effect on the weighting of reward or obligation. Interestingly, impulsivity, which correlated positively with apathy, was associated with an underweighting of effort. Hierarchical drift diffusion modelling supported these findings: apathy and impulsivity modulated the influence of effort on drift rate in opposite directions, altering evidence accumulation toward or away from high-effort options. Overall, these results suggest that everyday decisions depend on the integration of a wide range of value attributes and that apathy is associated with a selective overweighting of the perceived cost of effort.

title: Iron dysregulation: implications for pathology in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: In neurological diseases including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease and multiple sclerosis, iron overload is a major contributor to oxidative stress and localized injury. Iron can also cause harm through oxidative stress-independent mechanisms such as protein aggregation and abnormal sphingolipid metabolism. Dysregulation of iron homeostasis may occur systemically or within specific tissues, leading to deficiency, overload or intracellular mislocalization. These alterations disrupt cellular functions and contribute to disease pathology. Iron's ability to accept and donate electrons is essential for oxygen transport, energy production and DNA synthesis, yet this same reactivity also renders it potentially toxic, as excess iron promotes cellular damage including ferroptosis. Despite extensive research into the functions of iron under physiological conditions and its toxicity when dysregulated, critical questions remain unanswered. Why is iron homeostasis disrupted in the brain? What are the underlying mechanisms driving this dysregulation, and how can the resulting damage be mitigated or reversed? These questions are especially pertinent in the context of demyelinating and neurodegenerative disorders, where iron accumulation is a common pathological feature. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of iron biology, emphasizing its chemical properties, cellular functions, and the tightly regulated mechanisms that maintain iron homeostasis. We then discuss the pathological consequences of iron dysregulation in multiple sclerosis and the therapeutic strategies that have been developed to target iron toxicity. While the disease of prominence for this review is multiple sclerosis, we refer to countering iron in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease to highlight the approaches undertaken to ameliorate iron neurotoxicity.

title: ERK3 regulates metabolic memory-related arterial endothelial dysfunction through glutamate.
abstract: Endothelial dysfunction persisting after glucose normalization, termed metabolic memory, constitutes a primary driver of diabetic vascular complications, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The atypical mitogen‑activated protein kinase ERK3 has been implicated in metabolic regulation, but its role in the vascular endothelium under diabetic conditions is unknown. We found that the protein levels of ERK3 in endothelial cells were markedly attenuated following high glucose exposure and failed to rebound upon subsequent glucose normalization. Integrated metabolomic profiling coupled with downstream experiments revealed that ERK3 regulated NO through glutamate-mGluR2 pathway. Endothelial-specific ERK3 knockout aggravated arterial endothelial injury in db/db mice with or without insulin treatment, which can be blocked by mGluR2 inhibitors. Our findings identify ERK3 as a critical regulator of endothelial metabolic memory via the glutamate‑mGluR2‑NO pathway. This novel mechanism expands the current understanding of metabolic memory and highlights ERK3 and its downstream glutamate axis as potential therapeutic targets for preventing or reversing diabetic vascular complications.

title: Necrotising enterocolitis triggers a TNF-driven gut-blood-brain cascade that disrupts the blood-brain barrier and induces TNFR1-skewed neuronal apoptosis and pyroptosis.
abstract: Necrotising enterocolitis (NEC) in very-low-birthweight (VLBW) infants is associated with neurodevelopmental difficulties, but the mechanisms linking intestinal disease to brain injury remain unclear. We asked whether NEC propagates along a tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α)-centred gut-blood-brain pathway that compromises the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and activates inflammatory neuronal death programmes. In a retrospective cohort, inflammatory biomarkers at symptom onset (C-reactive protein and procalcitonin) were related to Bayley-III composite scores at 24 months' corrected age. We then used a neonatal rat NEC model with daily oral etanercept, a soluble TNF receptor fusion protein, or saline from postnatal day 2 to day 14 to assess intestinal histopathology and permeability, circulating microbial products, inflammation, BBB permeability, early neurobehaviour, microglial activation, and neuronal apoptosis and pyroptosis with TNF receptor (TNFR) localisation. An intestinal-epithelial cell-primary cortical neuron transwell co-culture tested whether LPS-injured epithelium was sufficient to release TNF-α, disrupt barrier integrity, and injure neurons, and whether etanercept mitigated these effects. In infants, higher C-reactive protein and procalcitonin at NEC onset were associated with lower Bayley-III motor, cognitive, and language scores. In rats, NEC caused small-intestinal injury with tight-junction loss and permeability, elevated circulating microbial products and TNF-α, increased BBB leak, activated microglia, and induced neuronal apoptosis and pyroptosis with a TNFR1-skewed and TNFR2-reduced profile. NEC also impaired early sensorimotor performance, and worse performance was associated with higher circulating C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, and TNF-α. Etanercept reduced inflammatory burden, improved intestinal and BBB integrity, and improved sensorimotor performance. In co-culture, LPS activated epithelial NF-κB and MAPK signalling, increased epithelial TNF-α, and reduced barrier resistance. Neurons exposed to this inflammatory milieu showed TNFR1 upregulation, TNFR2 downregulation, activation of apoptotic effectors, and NLRP1 inflammasome-linked pyroptotic signalling, accompanied by synaptic injury. Etanercept blunted upstream epithelial signalling, preserved barrier function, and reduced TNFR1-skewed neuronal injury programmes. Acute inflammatory burden at presentation tracked with poorer 24-month neurodevelopment, and experimental data support TNF signalling as a plausible, modifiable relay linking barrier failure to BBB dysfunction, microglial activation, and TNFR1-skewed neuronal injury. These findings support risk stratification using routine biomarkers and motivate mechanism-informed trials targeting inflammatory amplification in NEC.
keywords: Receptors, Tumor Necrosis Factor, Type I

title: Effect of remote ischemic conditioning on cerebral blood flow regulation in patients with ischemic stroke: a randomized, controlled trial.
abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a major contributor to long-term disability despite current therapies. Although remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) has potential benefits in patients with AIS, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We aimed to explore the effects of RIC on the regulation of cerebral blood flow (CBF) among patients with AIS. This was a randomized controlled trial with participant-and-blinded endpoints that included 120 patients with AIS from June 2023 to May 2024. RIC/sham RIC treatment was performed at a pressure of 200 mmHg or 60 mmHg twice a day for seven consecutive days. The primary efficacy outcome was the difference in CBF regulation 7 days after randomization between the two groups. Patients were followed up for 90 days after randomization to assess modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores. One hundred and twenty (120) patients with AIS were included in the intention-to-treat population (60 in each group). The results showed that the phase difference, which is a key parameter of CBF regulation, in the RIC group was significantly higher than that in the sham RIC group [affected side: RIC group: 36.84° (interquartile range [IQR], 21.49° to 51.36°), sham RIC group: 28.57° (17.17°, 38.52°), adjusted β coefficient = 11.336, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 4.523-18.149, P = 0.001; unaffected side: RIC group: 35.13° (20.77°, 56.51°), sham RIC group: 30.37° (15.65°, 40.11°), adjusted β coefficient = 11.780, 95% CI = 4.260-19.300, P = 0.002]. Additionally, there were no statistically significant differences in the secondary outcomes including blood pressure, heart rate, cerebral blood flow velocity in the middle cerebral artery, and 90-day mRS scores between the two groups (P > 0.05). RIC treatment did not increase adverse events during hospitalization. RIC can significantly improve CBF regulation in patients with AIS, which may be an intermediate mechanism by which it benefits this patient population. Clinical Trial Number: NCT05915832, Clinical Trial Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, Registration Date: 2023-06-23.

title: Oxytocin regulates consensus assessment in zebrafish social decision-making.
abstract: Group-living animals can gain information from conspecifics and integrate it in behavioural decisions that increase their survival. Social information value depends on two key dimensions: salience, the perceptual prominence of social signals, and conformity, the tendency to follow the majority based on the appraisal of signal consensus amongst conspecifics. Here we tested the effects of oxytocin, a neuromodulator conserved across vertebrates, on salience and conformity processing of conspecific alarm behaviours, using zebrafish oxytocin-receptor (oxtr-/-) knockout mutants. We employed video-playback treatments to independently manipulate the absolute number (salience) and relative proportion (consensus) of alarm signals against matched neutral controls. Knocking out oxtr eliminated increased attention to higher signal salience observed in wild-type siblings but did not alter behavioural responses. In contrast, receptor loss abolished conformity to majority alarm signals, eliminating consensus-dependent increases in social contagion and subsequent social approach. Predictive models further revealed that oxytocin enables feedback from immediate social responses to shape later decisions, specifically when social information is corroborated by the majority. These findings challenge the prevailing view that oxytocin primarily enhances social salience, expanding its role to the assessment of consensus to implement conformity decisions, representing a foundational process in vertebrate social decision-making.

title: Predicting response to electroconvulsive therapy combined with antipsychotics in patients with schizophrenia using insula-related functional connectivity: an interoceptive theory-driven analysis.
abstract: Variability in electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) response among patients with schizophrenia and the risks of ineffective treatment limit its clinical use. Identifying reliable predictors to accurately forecast patient response to ECT continues to be a major challenge. This study aimed to investigate whether insula-related functional connectivity features (FCs), grounded in interoceptive dysfunction theory, can accurately predict ECT-antipsychotics (APs) combination outcomes in schizophrenia and identify reliable predictors and potential neural mechanisms of ECT-APs. Forty-five patients with schizophrenia, either treatment-resistant or in an acute exacerbation, underwent MRI and clinical assessments at baseline and after 4-weeks of ECT-APs treatment in this single-center proof-of-concept study. Based on interoceptive dysfunction theory, baseline insula-related FCs were extracted to train a machine learning model for predicting the change in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale scores (PANSS%) within a nested cross-validation framework. We also identified the functional connectivity patterns of responders and explored potential neural targets of ECT-APs. Cross-validation of the optimal model revealed that 16 baseline insula-related FCs significantly predicted post-ECT-APs changes in PANSS(%) scores (r[predicted vs. observed] = 0.93, p < 0.001). These features involved FCs between the insula (ventral anterior and posterior) and large-scale networks encompassing frontal, temporal, limbic, thalamic, and cerebellar regions. Among them, three FCs showed significant post-ECT-APs changes that were associated with symptom improvement, suggesting dual roles as predictors and potential therapeutic targets involving salience-auditory-interoceptive circuits. Others, such as insula-cerebellar Crus II and insula-precuneus connections, distinguished responders and non-responders but less modifiable by ECT-APs. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the predictive value of insula-related functional connectivity in ECT-APs response; future multi-center studies are needed to confirm generalizability. Not applicable.

title: The diagnostic and therapeutic potential of palmitoylation-related genes in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a highly heterogeneous disorder, for which early accurate diagnosis and subtype stratification remain clinically challenging. Palmitoylation, a critical reversible post‑translational modification, has been implicated in the pathological progression of AD. However, a comprehensive investigation of palmitoylation‑related pathway genes in the context of AD diagnosis and molecular subtyping is still lacking. Transcriptomic data from three AD cohorts in the GEO database were integrated and corrected for batch effects. Palmitoylation‑related differentially expressed genes (PR‑DEGs) were screened through differential expression analysis combined with weighted gene co‑expression network analysis (WGCNA). Based on these PR‑DEGs, molecular subtyping, pathway enrichment, and immune infiltration analyses were performed in AD. Twelve machine learning algorithms were employed to construct 113 classification models, and core palmitoylation‑related biomarkers with stable cross‑cohort performance were identified via multi‑algorithm cross‑screening. Model generalizability was validated using two independent external GEO datasets (GSE132903 and GSE138260). In addition, SHAP analysis, single‑cell transcriptomics, regulatory network construction, and drug prediction were integrated to elucidate the biological functions and clinical potential of the core genes. In this study, 15 core PR‑DEGs were identified, and AD was stratified into two heterogeneous subtypes: subtype C1, whose palmitoylation profile resembled that of normal aging, and subtype C2, which exhibited pronounced palmitoylation suppression, synaptic impairment, and immune dysregulation. A random forest model constructed based on the PR‑DEGs demonstrated stable and excellent diagnostic performance, with consistently high area under the curve (AUC) values across multiple cohorts. Six core diagnostic genes were further screened, among which CHRM1 showed the highest diagnostic value and model contribution, along with a neuron‑specific aberrant expression pattern. These core genes exhibited coordinated dysregulation and were implicated in multiple AD‑relevant pathways, including synaptic homeostasis, lipid metabolism, Wnt signaling, and neuroinflammation. In addition, several potential targeted therapeutic agents were predicted. In this study, a preliminary machine learning‑based diagnostic and subtype stratification analytic framework for AD was constructed based on the palmitoylation pathway. Bioinformatics analyses suggested that core genes, including CHRM1, PORCN, CRMP1, GNG3, CLIP3and ACOT7, may hold promise as potential biomarkers for precise diagnosis and targeted intervention in AD, thereby providing a theoretical reference for early screening, personalized mechanistic investigation, and therapeutic exploration.

title: Patient perspectives from the BEYOND Delphi panel: burden of remaining symptoms and their fluctuations, despite treatment, in patients with generalised myasthenia gravis.
abstract: Patients with generalised myasthenia gravis (gMG) can experience remaining symptoms despite treatment. Our study aimed to describe how remaining symptoms and their fluctuations may affect a person's daily life while living with gMG. A modified-Delphi panel (two survey rounds) was conducted with adult patients with gMG (n=20) from seven European countries (France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK). A scientific advisory committee including two neurologists and three patient advocacy group representatives guided the study. Consensus was defined as ≥80% participants in agreement (rated 7‒9 on a 9-point Likert scale) on a particular statement. Participants receiving a range of gMG treatments highlighted the personal and variable impacts of remaining symptoms in five key domains: daily activities, social life, mental wellbeing, work and education, and future plans. Across all domains, >40% of participants declared a high impact (rating 7-9 on Likert scale), with the highest proportion of patients declaring a high impact in the mental wellbeing domain (63%). Adjustments to daily activities, evening plans, working hours or even career moves, were frequently noted impacts of remaining symptoms and fluctuations. Participants also mentioned loss of independence and fears about forthcoming symptom severity as impactful. One statement reached consensus in agreement: "if my symptoms were better controlled, I would have greater freedom to do the things I enjoy and lead a more satisfying life". This study is the first to investigate the specific impacts of remaining symptoms of gMG on patients' daily lives and how fluctuations may contribute to this impact. These results demonstrate the burden of these remaining symptoms for patients, suggesting that more effective therapeutic strategies leading to more sustained disease control would likely improve patients' daily lives.

title: Glymphatic system dysfunction in anti-NMDAR encephalitis: a comparative DTI-ALPS study with healthy controls and epilepsy patients.
abstract: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is characterized by pathogenic autoantibody-mediated synaptic dysfunction, yet the mechanisms facilitating antibody access to the brain parenchyma remain incompletely understood. The glymphatic system, which supports cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange along perivascular spaces, has been implicated in immune surveillance and waste clearance; however, its involvement in anti-NMDAR encephalitis has not been fully investigated in vivo. Glymphatic system-related function was assessed using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) in 15 patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis, 17 patients with epilepsy, and 18 healthy controls. Group differences in ALPS-index values were analyzed with adjustment for age and sex. Associations between ALPS-indexes, clinical severity, and regional brain volumes were further examined. ALPS-index values were significantly reduced in both anti-NMDAR encephalitis and epilepsy compared with healthy controls. Across all groups, ALPS-indexes demonstrated strong bilateral correlations, with consistently lower values in the right hemisphere. In anti-NMDAR encephalitis, lower ALPS-index values were associated with longer hospitalization and higher modified Rankin Scale scores, whereas no associations were observed with cerebrospinal fluid anti-NMDAR antibody titers. In epilepsy, ALPS-indexes showed a distinct pattern of clinical and structural correlations, including associations with regional brain volumes that were absent in the NMDAR group. Receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated moderate-to-good discriminative performance of ALPS-indexes for both disease groups. DTI-ALPS reveals altered perivascular water diffusivity in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, which correlates with clinical severity independently of antibody titers. These findings suggest glymphatic-related dysfunction in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, and indicate that the ALPS-index captures disease-relevant pathophysiological processes beyond antibody burden, with potential utility as a noninvasive imaging marker for clinical assessment and prognosis in immune-mediated encephalitis.

title: Signal mining and safety profile analysis of prucalopride: a pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS) database.
abstract: Prucalopride is a highly selective 5-HT4 agonist used for chronic idiopathic constipation and gastroparesis. Although clinical trials suggest a favorable safety profile, real-world data on rare adverse events (AEs) remain scarce. This study mined the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) to detect safety signals warranting clinical attention. FAERS data from December 14, 2018 to September 30, 2025 were collected via OpenVigil 2.1. AEs were categorised using the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities. Signal detection was performed using four specific algorithms: the Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR), the Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR), the Multi-item Gamma Poisson Shrinker (MGPS), and the Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network (BCPNN). Kappa consistency and sensitivity analyses were performed. We collected 1101 prucalopride-related reports and identified 35 positive adverse drug event (ADE) signals across 10 system organ classes. Gastrointestinal disorders dominated (12 signals, 373 cases), followed by psychiatric disorders (9 signals, 107 cases) and nervous system disorders (5 signals, 181 cases). Frequent reactions included headache, diarrhoea, nausea, dizziness and abdominal pain. Signal intensity varied across algorithms; gastrointestinal bacterial overgrowth emerged as a strong signal in all four. We found 19 ADEs that were not listed in the prescribing information of China, the United States, or Europe; serious unlabeled signals included intestinal obstruction and serotonin syndrome. Notably, depression, suicidal ideation, depressed mood, and nightmares appear only in the United States prescribing information. Prucalopride-related ADEs involve multiple organ systems, predominantly presenting as gastrointestinal disorders, psychiatric disorders and nervous system disorders. Some ADEs not included in the instructions may be serious adverse events, require great attention from clinicians. For patients with underlying comorbidities or those undergoing combination therapy, close monitoring for potential severe adverse events is essential to ensure clinical medication safety.
keywords: United States Food and Drug Administration

title: Therapeutic regimen for AD-derived MCI: the effect of sodium oligomannate (GV-971) combined with donepezil on patients' cognitive function and hippocampal atrophy rate.
abstract: To investigate the clinical efficacy of sodium oligomannate (GV-971) combined with donepezil in the treatment of patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in Alzheimer's disease (AD). This non-randomized, open-label, retrospective analytic study included 100 patients with AD-derived MCI who were treated in our hospital between May 2023 and May 2024, and were divided into two groups according to the different treatment modalities recorded in the electronic medical record system: 44 cases in the control group (donepezil), and 56 cases in the observation group (sodium oligomannate (GV-971) combined with donepezil). Cognitive function, biochemical markers (homocysteine (Hcy), S100 calcium binding protein B (S100β), neuron-specific enolase (NSE)), serum intestinal flora metabolic markers (phenylalanine (Phe), short-chain fatty acids (SCFA), γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), acetylcholine (Ach)), hippocampal volume, and adverse effects were collected and compared between the two groups, and adverse reactions were recorded. After treatment, the comparison of various scores of cognitive function, Hcy, S100β, NSE, Phe, SCFA, GABA, and Ach between the patients in the observation group and the control group showed statistically significant differences (P0.05). In contrast, the calculated hippocampal atrophy rate-derived from the percentage change relative to baseline volume-was significantly lower in the observation group than in the control group (P 0.05). The combination of sodium oligomannate (GV-971) and donepezil was associated with more favorable changes in cognitive function, neuronal injury biomarkers, serum markers of gut microbiota metabolism, and a slower observed rate of hippocampal atrophy in patients with AD-derived MCI. These associations do not imply causation, and the combination regimen did not significantly increase adverse reactions in this cohort.

title: Effect of low-dose esketamine on quality of recovery after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Although low-dose esketamine has shown analgesic benefits, its effect on the quality of recovery after gynecologic laparoscopy remains unclear. In this double-blind randomized controlled trial, 140 adults with ASA I-II and a BMI of 18.5-30 kg/m² undergoing elective gynecologic laparoscopy (hysterectomy, myomectomy, or ovarian cystectomy) were randomly assigned to Group E (esketamine group) or Group C (control group). Patients in Group E received 0.25 mg/kg esketamine bolus after anesthesia induction followed by a continuous infusion of 0.1 mg/kg/h until 15 min before the end of surgery, whereas those in Group C received an equal volume of normal saline. The primary outcome was the total score on the Quality of Recovery-40 questionnaire (QoR-40) at 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) scores at rest and during activity at 0, 6, 12, and 24 h postoperatively, tracheal extubation time, rescue analgesic consumption, and the incidences of nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and nightmares. Group E had significantly higher global QoR-40 scores than Group C at 24 h postoperatively (adjusted mean difference 2.30, 95% CI 0.21 to 4.39; P = 0.034). Pain scores at rest and during activity were lower in Group E at 6 h (rest: mean (SD), 2.28 (1.69) vs. 3.01 (2.09), P = 0.025; activity: 3.03 (1.80) vs. 3.81 (2.08), P = 0.020) and 24 h (rest: 1.88 (1.30) vs. 2.29 (1.32), P = 0.045; activity: 2.56 (1.43) vs. 3.16 (1.60), P = 0.022), but were comparable between groups at 0 h and 12 h. The incidence of dizziness was significantly higher in Group E than in Group C during the PACU period (23.5% vs. 8.7%; risk difference (RD) 14.8%, 95% CI 2.8% to 26.9%; P = 0.033). However, this difference resolved by 24 h postoperatively (25.0% vs. 23.2%; P = 0.962), and no significant differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Low-dose esketamine was associated with a statistically higher QoR-40 score, but the magnitude was below the Minimum Clinically Important Difference (MCID) and therefore may not represent a clinically meaningful improvement in gynecologic laparoscopy. The trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trials Registry ( www.chictr.org.cn , registration number: ChiCTR2300072538, date of registration: 16/06/2023).

title: Alzheimer's disease and cancer as opposing failures of APP signaling network homeostasis: from pleiotropic components to multi-target therapeutics.
abstract: The inverse epidemiological relationship between Alzheimer's disease (AD) and cancer has been previously explained by a "Cleavage Pathway Imbalance" in amyloid precursor protein (APP) proteolysis. Here we expand this model into a dynamic, multi-dimensional APP signaling network that integrates extracellular cues, intracellular adaptors, organelle-contact dynamics, and proteolytic events. In AD, the network undergoes catastrophic post-mitotic collapse, driven by endolysosomal dysfunction, impaired autophagy, and downstream mitochondrial failure, resulting in synaptic degeneration. In cancer, the same network is hijacked to sustain proliferative, invasive, and immunoevasive programs. Crucially, network components such as BACE1 and ADAM10 act as neurodegenerative drivers in the brain yet as oncogenic promoters in peripheral tissues. We advocate a shift from reductionist single-pathway inhibition to rational, multi-target strategies that restore system-wide network homeostasis. Embracing this context-aware, network-based framework is essential for developing safer and more effective therapeutics for these two major age-related disorders.

title: Ephaptic coupling between neurons: a systematic review of mathematical models.
abstract: Ephaptic coupling is a relatively underexplored mechanism of neuronal interaction mediated by perturbations of the extracellular electric potential without the formation of conventional chemical or electrical synapses. Although the first theoretical accounts of ephaptic interactions appeared as early as the 1940s, computational approaches to this phenomenon have been actively developed only since the late 1990s and early 2000s, based on classical models of neuronal activity and cable theory. Both simplified phenomenological and biophysically detailed models have been developed. The former capture only essential features of large-scale neuronal dynamics and offer high computational efficiency, whereas the latter incorporate more complex characteristics, such as the properties of myelinated and unmyelinated fibers, the spatial distribution of nodes of Ranvier, axonal diameter heterogeneity, and the dynamics of extracellular ion concentrations. Recent studies highlight a growing interest in ephaptic interactions, particularly in their potential roles in neuronal synchronization, sensory coding, the propagation of epileptic seizures, and the development of neurodegenerative as well as demyelinating disorders. This work presents the systematic review dedicated to mathematical models of ephaptic coupling. The review aims to consolidate the diverse computational approaches used to study ephaptic coupling and to outline the main mechanisms of this phenomenon explored in modeling studies. The reviewed models were classified by type, tested hypotheses, and availability of open-source implementations. We surveyed nearly seventy mathematical models of ephaptic coupling. The review highlights how ephaptic interactions may contribute not only to normal brain function-such as synchronization and sensory processing-but also to pathological conditions, including epilepsy, demyelination, neuropathic pain, and neurodegeneration. By bringing together disparate studies, we aim to make the modeling of ephaptic coupling comprehensible to a broad scientific audience, including researchers with little prior experience in this area, stimulate further integration of computational and experimental approaches, and promote investigation of ephaptic mechanisms in both health and disease. This review serves both as a reference point for researchers developing new computational models and as a resource for those seeking to understand how ephaptic interactions may shape neuronal dynamics.

title: Primary Care Continuity During the Transition to Adulthood and Its Association With Acute Healthcare Utilization Among Youth With Eating Disorders.
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: The transition from pediatric to adult care is a high-risk period for youth with eating disorders (EDs), often characterized by care disruptions and disengagement from adult services. This study examined whether patterns of primary care continuity during this transition are associated with acute healthcare utilization post-transition. A retrospective cohort study of 1106 youth discharged from a tertiary pediatric ED program in Ontario, Canada. Primary care continuity was categorized into five groups based on dominant general practitioner (GP) patterns before and after age 18. Outcomes included emergency department visits (EDVs) and hospitalizations within 2 years post-transition. Multivariate logistic regression models estimated associations, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors, and corresponding pre-transition acute healthcare utilization. Compared with maintaining the same dominant GP before and after age 18 (Group 1), no dominant GP in either period (Group 5) was associated with lower odds of any EDV (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.32-0.73), any hospitalization (OR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.16-0.76), and MH-related hospitalization (OR: 0.30, 95% CI: 0.08-0.81). A dominant GP before but not after 18 (Group 4) was associated with lower odds of MH-related EDVs (OR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.29-0.95). Sensitivity analyses generally supported these findings. Primary care continuity was not associated with acute healthcare utilization among youth with EDs, highlighting a complex relationship between GP continuity, healthcare needs, and healthcare use. Lower utilization among those without a dominant GP may not indicate lower need or better outcomes. Future research should clarify these patterns, while transition planning should continue to support timely and sustained primary care involvement for youth with EDs.

title: Continuous multimodal neuromonitoring of zolpidem-induced paradoxical awakening in chronic incomplete locked-in syndrome: ventral pontine deafferentation, cross-modal complementarity, and cardio-cortical dissociation.
abstract: Zolpidem paradoxically restores responsiveness in select disorders of consciousness (DOC) cases, yet real-time electrophysiological and autonomic dynamics across the pharmacodynamic trajectory remain uncharacterized in incomplete locked-in syndrome (LIS). A 52.18-min multimodal recording tracked baseline, enteral zolpidem administration (min 22.39), absorption, corticomotor peak, and plateau in a 42-year-old male with chronic LIS from pontine infarction. Analytics included continuous qEEG (0.5-70 Hz), microstates (Classes A-D), beta-band weighted Phase Lag Index (wPLI) connectomics, heart rate variability (HRV), and heartbeat‑evoked responses (HER). Baseline deafferentation showed severe theta slowing (48.36 ± 4.14%) and phase hypersynchrony. Following enteral administration, the following changes were observed: 1. viscero-cortical dissociation: Infusion triggered an immediate HRV VHF surge (>80%) while the cortex remained quiescent for 14.1 min. 2. Corticomotor consolidation: Between min 36.5-46.0, relative beta surged (+266.89%) while theta dropped (-30.74%). Microstates accelerated into frontocentral Classes C/D, and connectomics demonstrated long-range edge pruning with selective frontocentral recruitment (wPLI > 0.40). 3. Interoceptive gating: During peak beta emergence, cardio-cortical communication collapsed; evoked global variance profile dropped > 60% (1.03 to 0.22 µV) alongside frontocentral dipole suppression. Paradoxical awakening is a coordinated multisystem process. Zolpidem disinhibits spared corticomotor networks while filtering ascending visceral baro-afferents, enabling an outward-facing behavioral state decoupled from internal interoception.
